app.title: AlgaTwin / Virtual Photobioreactor
app.summary: A person uploads growth measurements over time from one or more culture runs, or picks a labelled synthetic example. A six-step guide takes them through mapping columns and units, confirming replicate ids, choosing a growth model, and typing in every fixed parameter, initial condition, search bound and noise level. They then fit the shared parameters across runs and check which ones the data can actually pin down (identifiability). If they want, they can also measure error on held-out runs. They finish with a report in HTML, PDF or JSON that states each estimate, interval and flag. A second workspace lets them simulate the calibrated model under new light, nutrient and path settings, save and compare scenarios, look at the light field and parameter sensitivities, and search a grid of conditions for candidate experiments.

task.text: Calibrate a mechanistic growth model against time-course culture measurements, find out which parameters the data can identify, and report the result or use the model to explore new conditions.

data.text: Long or wide tables of biomass and nutrient concentrations measured over time in several culture runs with technical replicates, plus explicit model parameters and run conditions.
data.item: one measurement of biomass or nutrient at one time point in one culture run

stage.text: fitting a growth model to cultivation measurements after the runs are done, before reporting or planning the next experiment

mechanism.text: A stepped guide with a progress bar unlocks each stage only after the one before is complete. Editable tables collect the model's parameters, conditions, bounds and noise levels, and any change to the inputs clears the results that depended on them. After the fit, overlaid line charts of observed and modelled values sit beside an estimates table and the report downloads. In the baseline workspace, tabs share one active parameter set across simulation sliders, a light heatmap, a sensitivity bar chart and a scatter of the planning grid.

field.text: ODE growth-kinetics calibration with profile likelihood in microalgal bioprocess modelling

workflow.name: fit a dynamic model to time-course measurements and report which parameters are identifiable

steps.here: upload a wide CSV of culture measurements, using a blank template if needed, and declare whether it is measured or synthetic; or choose the synthetic worked example

steps.step: map columns and units, then confirm them
steps.here: map columns for time, biomass (or a calibrated proxy), elemental N, quota, run id and replicate id, and pick their units; a confirm checkbox must be ticked before the model step

steps.step: specify the model and every assumption
steps.here: pick the nutrient model, light response and options, then fill editable tables of parameter values, initial conditions per run, search bounds for the fitted parameters and fixed noise SDs; nothing is filled in for you

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: fit the shared parameters and recompute profile likelihoods, which withhold parameters that are not identifiable; leave-one-whole-run-out held-out error can be computed when there are at least two runs
read plain-language flags, the estimates table and observed-vs-model curves, then download HTML, PDF and JSON reports, the reusable model job and the mapped observations

steps.step: explore what-if scenarios with the fitted model
steps.here: sliders for light, nitrogen, path and duration redraw the simulated curves; named scenarios are saved and overlaid; a light × nitrogen grid marks non-dominated candidate experiments

distinctive: Parameters whose likelihood profiles are flat or open are labelled NOT IDENTIFIABLE, and their estimates and intervals are withheld
in-sample error and leave-one-whole-run-out held-out error are always reported separately
every input is hashed, so changing the data, mapping or model clears the downstream fit and report
the data origin (measured or synthetic) is declared and kept, and a measured upload cannot use a synthetic conversion
a Beer–Lambert self-shading heatmap shows light at each depth over time
